- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.4), model tends to overcorrect downward; reduce forecast bias by 5–10% relative to recent highs.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +3%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots; cap forecast peak at 1.5x recent high or adjust downward by 2–3 points.
- If sentiment is positive and price is trending up, model frequently overestimates; apply a 1–2 point downward bias to avoid overconfidence.
- Mean reversion is strong in 3–5 day horizons; if forecast is >2σ above recent 10-day mean, reduce by 10–15%.
- In 30-day forecasts, model often ignores sentiment momentum; if sentiment has trended consistently positive over last 5 days, add 0.5–1.0 point upward bias.
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed, model tends to forecast mid-range; use 3–5 day moving average of history as baseline, then adjust ±0.5–1.0 based on sentiment volatility.
